# Elora

> Elora is a local-first AI companion for Windows 10 and 11. Conversation, optional screen context, dated memory, reminders and owner-directed actions share a desktop workspace. English and Roman Urdu are supported. Product information reviewed 13 October 2026.

## Core and connected features

- The background brain, vision, embeddings and memory storage stay local. Ollama serves local language, vision and embedding models; speech uses separate local engines.
- Chat, speech recognition and voice are local by default. Each can use GroqCloud in hybrid mode, with local fallback on failure. Selected audio, chat context or text to speak then leaves the device.
- Push-to-talk is the default interaction. Optional hands-free mode keeps the microphone open for a local name check; meeting audio capture is separate.
- Optional Windows desktop control requires Windows-MCP, Groq and hybrid mode. It runs only on owner requests. System operations require approval. Focused-window text may go to Groq; screenshots do not.
- Google Workspace connects Gmail, Calendar and Drive after OAuth setup. Reads can run automatically; writes and deletes require HUD approval. Google content used by cloud chat or voice may also reach Groq.
- Hermes hands is experimental and off by default. It needs a compatible model served with at least 64K context; the baseline 8K model does not qualify. The optional code hand needs Docker.
- Local memory includes SQLite, vector recall and versioned memory blocks. Conversation and background memory integration are still being improved.
- Requirements: Windows 10/11, 16 GB RAM minimum (32–64 GB more comfortable). Tuned on a 4 GB GTX 1650; model choice affects hardware needs. Source setup uses Python 3.13, Ollama and Node.js.
- Availability: active development. This website has no public installer or active email waitlist. Commercial pricing is not announced here.
- The intelligence scorecard is a historical 4 October 2026 snapshot, not a current benchmark. It was not rerun for this site update.
